deviations: Identity access has no export link: PH-304 freezes only four CSV datasets (ops_overview/settlement_coverage/cash_bridge/fee_pairing) and deliberately excludes identity-sensitive token/password details; the workbench therefore returns export=null + export_missing=['export_dataset_not_implemented'] for identity_access instead of inventing a new export format (PH-310 is the follow-up for new formats).

PM cash export is unavailable: cash facts carry no project attribution (same limitation disclosed by PH-279/PH-288/PH-309), so the cash_bridge partition exposes export=null + export_missing=['permission'] for pm rather than leaking company-wide cash.

The linkage reuses the existing PH-304 ops-export/ named service and canonical history_read route; no new route, metadata copy, POST/write channel, table, migration or audit write is introduced. The export still uses PH-304's request_token semantics and zero-audit default.
The workbench template builds export links from dataset/as_of/period descriptors; the export page links back to the workbench, but both pages remain GET-only history_read.

No business rule is re-derived: partition metrics come from the PH-309 aggregation and CSV rows from the PH-304 composition of the same owner read services; consistency is asserted for the settlement partition row count vs its open_item_count metric.
Counterexamples/tests never UPDATE/DELETE historical rows; the linkage itself is read-only, so append-only triggers are untouched.

Single worker owns the whole write set (workbench service/view/templates/domain metadata, delivery urls, two test files, governance); no parallel slice writes these files; independent review is pending.
